newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes weaker and tests support.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes weaker and tests support.

text.p: The precious metals lost further value on Tuesday after prices were chased lower by trade selling shortly after the New York markets opened, dealers said.
"The whole sector is looking relatively sickly but whether it's weak enough to go lower we'll have to see," a dealers said.

Silver led the way down from New York after some early covering of short positions on the Comex futures market gave way to trade and speculative selling which in turn triggered sell orders from computer-controlled investment programmes.
Gold was testing its chart-based technical support after opening lower following selling overnight, probably on behalf of gold producers, dealers said.

"The downtrend resistance line is at $384.95, so that is the break-out point. There is scope to test it, but I would be looking for a failure," said Karen Jones, technical analyst at Credit Suisse in London.
Gold was fixed at $381.70 per ounce after $382.35 at the morning fix and $382.90 on Monday afternoon.

"Silver was the main mover in New York and it looks a bit shaky," a dealers said. "There was a good bid early on Comex which brought in some short covering, but after it was withdrawn, it came off again."
Dealers said some selling was related to the expiry of "over the counter" (OTC) on Tuesday afternoon.
Gold and silver prices were lower at the expiry but they were still away from the most favoured option prices.
An option gives its owner the right to buy or sell a commodity at a given price at a given future date.
Most recent option dealing has been tactical and done to protect the holder against sudden price moves rather than take a view aimed at making a profit on the market.
Selling pressure may be offset slightly by the start of the peak demand time for gold, due to top consumer India's forthcoming Diwali festival of lights and wedding season.
Silver was also easier at $4.84/$4.86 an ounce, a decline of eight cents from Monday's London close.
But platinum and palladium looked even weaker with platinum hovering close to par with gold since Friday for the first time nearly three years. It was off $2.50 at $381.75/$382.75
A week ago platinum was at around a $2 premium to gold.
Palladium also looked weak, probing recent lows at $114.85/$115.85 an ounce, down $1.15 from Monday's close.
